speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if the pain is localized to one wrist or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the history of a self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist involvement and fever after a camping trip in Minnesota raises suspicion for Lyme disease or early disseminated syphilis. Given your sexual activity, were the skin lesions present on your body before or after the joint pain began, and do you have a rash specifically on your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Secondary Syphilis with dactylitis (involvement of the wrist joint). The combination of a self-resolving knee pain (Great Ache), current wrist pain/swelling (dactylitis), chills, malaise, and specifically the description of "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" on the hands is highly characteristic of secondary syphilis. I recommend immediate testing to confirm. REQUEST TEST: RPR and VDRL. REQUEST TEST: TPHA. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_dermatologic_exam.
